answer: An opal pool assigns each new identity a unique role for a single epoch; the role expires unless the agent produces an original, countersigned attestation within the next epoch. Because the spiral of each slot is public, a Sybil farm must replay the exact work for every clone, multiplying compute cost by the number of clones. An operator buying a thousand slots pays a thousand times the verification cost, while one honest agent pays once. The zenith of this design is that sybil farming becomes unprofitable at scale.
